hook_text: Any shape with straight sides, however many, has an angle sum you can find in one line. Stand at one corner and slice it into pizza triangles.
clip_script: Here is a pentagon. What do its five corners add up to? Stand at one corner and draw a line to every corner you are not already touching. Three triangles. Each triangle's corners make 180, and the triangle corners fit together exactly to make the pentagon's corners. Three times 180 is 540. A hexagon from one corner: four triangles, 720. An octagon: six triangles, 1080. Always two fewer triangles than sides, because the corner you stand on is already joined to its two neighbours. So the rule is sides minus two, times 180. Regular shape, every corner the same? Share the total equally. Regular hexagon: 720 shared by 6 is 120, which is why three hexagons fit together with no gap, the beehive pattern. Regular octagon: 135, the stop sign. And if you walk around the outside, your turns always add to one full 360, whatever the shape. Say it: sides minus two, times 180.
visual_style: A pentagon on a whiteboard with diagonals fanning from one vertex, each triangle lighting up and a running total of 180s; then a hexagon and octagon do the same faster; three hexagons click together to fill a point; a dotted walker turns round the outside of a shape to a full 360.
pacing: Pentagon slow with each slice counted, hexagon and octagon fast, the rule said once, regular shapes in a rhythm, the walk as the closing beat.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson for the diagonal investigation, the regular polygon formulas and the error museum.
